(1) we introduce four methods for visualizing composition in NLP models, (2) these methods can be applied to simple recurrent nets and LSTM, (3) we show that simple recurrent nets are not capable of compositionality, and (4) the salience of a unit is proportional to its contribution to the final output.

(1) we can visualize compositionality of neural models using four simple methods, (2) negation and intensification are asymmetric, (3) LSTMs are more salient than simple recurrent nets, (4) LSTMs have more information flow than simple recurrent nets.
